messages.subject: RNG for Beta is Failing
parts:
Hi,

I'm finding that RNG for Beta is not passing the chi-squared goodness of fit test. I am using the following code:


    template <class RNG>
    inline double
    beta_rng(double alpha,
             double beta,
     RNG& rng1,
     RNG& rng2) {
      using boost::variate_generator;
      using boost::random::gamma_distribution;
      variate_generator<RNG&, gamma_distribution<> >
        rng_gamma_alpha(rng1, gamma_distribution<>(alpha, 1.0));
      variate_generator<RNG&, gamma_distribution<> >
        rng_gamma_beta(rng2, gamma_distribution<>(beta, 1.0));
      return rng_gamma_alpha() / (rng_gamma_alpha() + rng_gamma_beta());
    }

and test:

TEST(ProbDistributionsBeta, doesFit) {
  boost::random::mt19937 rng1, rng2;
  int N = 10000;
  int K = 5;
  boost::math::beta_distribution<>dist (2.0,2.0);
  boost::math::chi_squared mydist(K-1);

  double loc[4];
  for(int i = 1; i < K; i++)
    loc[i - 1] = quantile(dist, 0.2 * i);

  int count = 0;
  int bin [5] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0};

  while (count < N) {
    double a = stan::prob::beta_rng(2.0,2.0,rng1,rng2);
    int i = 0;
    while (i < K-1 && a > loc[i]) 
++i;
    ++bin[i];
    count++;
   }

  double chi = 0;
  double expect [5] = {N / K, N / K, N / K, N / K, N / K};

  for(int j = 0; j < K; j++)
    chi += ((bin[j] - expect[j]) * (bin[j] - expect[j]) / expect[j]);

  EXPECT_TRUE(chi < quantile(complement(mydist, 1e-6)));
}

I'm not sure what is going wrong; I took the beta dist. rv generation from wiki (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_distribution#Generating_beta-distributed_random_variates).

When I run the test, I get that the value of chi is 2120.29 which is not less than 33.3768 (qunatile(complement(mydist,1e-6))). 

However, when I decrease N to 100 or less, the test passes..



Thanks,
Peter

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RNG for Beta is Failing
parts:
You should only have a single rng for an argument
and use it twice.

My guess is that you're making two copies and that's
why it's failing. If you copy an RNG in Boost, it'll
create another one that generates the same random
number sequence.

Otherwise, you should just break things down and see
what's going on step by step in the algorithm.

- Bob

On 3/2/13 7:34 PM, Peter Li wrote:

> I'm finding that RNG for Beta is not passing the chi-squared goodness of fit test. I am using the following code:
>
>
> template <class RNG>
> inline double
> beta_rng(double alpha,
> double beta,
> RNG& rng1,
> RNG& rng2) {

You just wnat to use a single rng argument and pass it into
the constructor for rng_gamma_alpha and rng_gamma_beta.
The types look OK.

> using boost::variate_generator;
> using boost::random::gamma_distribution;
> variate_generator<RNG&, gamma_distribution<> >
> rng_gamma_alpha(rng1, gamma_distribution<>(alpha, 1.0));
> variate_generator<RNG&, gamma_distribution<> >
> rng_gamma_beta(rng2, gamma_distribution<>(beta, 1.0));
> return rng_gamma_alpha() / (rng_gamma_alpha() + rng_gamma_beta());

Also, instead of the last line, you need to do this:

double a = rng_gamma_alpha();
double b = rng_gamma_beta(0;

return a / (a + b);

You're drawing three random numbers here instead of two.

- Bob

Oh. Well, in R they are the same to at least 13 digits of precision

qchisq(ppoints(80), df = 79) - qchisq(1 - ppoints(80), df = 79, lower.tail = FALSE)

so I doubt it would make any difference to the tests.
